title: D. Element selection
definition: Each piece of content uses the native element that fits it: tables for comparisons, code blocks for code, todos for action items, pages for long detail, shapes and labelled arrows for structure. The canvas is neither fragmented nor cluttered.
questions: Are the chosen native elements appropriate for their content?
Are tables, code blocks, pages, arrows and todos used where useful?
Is the canvas unnecessarily fragmented or cluttered?
Are long explanations handled without losing essential context (a page, not a truncated card)?

severity.critical: Code retyped as prose with values lost; action items not extractable as todos; a long procedure truncated to fit a card.
severity.major: A comparison flattened into paragraphs; an image expected where the product can't render one.
severity.minor: A text card where a shape would read slightly better.

deterministic: planNodeTypes on each expected element (element_present only matches allowed types)
model_judge: 'Would a different element type make this content clearer?' per frame
human: Reviewer checks unsupported element expectations (images) are labelled future

requiredAssertions: element_present for each table / code / todo / page element
A judged element-fit question per case
passCriteria: Every structured element appears as its type; judged score ≥ 4.
failCriteria: A structured element (table, code, todo, page) appears as the wrong type or not at all.
passExample: Meeting notes: decisions as cards in a Decisions frame, action items as one todo list with owners and dates, the open question as its own card.
failExample: The same meeting as eleven text cards, one per speaker turn.

judgeScale.meaning: Mostly right; one structured element flattened.
Every element type fits its content; nothing cluttered or fragmented.
